name: Electric Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with two or three wheels, a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts. Session Law 2026-46 (HB 1094, signed July 7, 2026) sorts it into three classes from December 1, 2026: class 1 pedal assist and class 2 throttle, both to 20 mph, and class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph; until then its motor alone may not push it past 20 mph. Defined by N.C. Gen. Stat. §20-4.01(7a) and, from December 1, 2026, regulated by §20-171.3.
restrictions: Two or three wheels, a seat or saddle, fully operable pedals and a motor of no more than 750 watts
Until December 1, 2026, its top speed on motor power alone on level ground is 20 mph
From December 1, 2026, class 1 assists only while the rider is pedaling and class 2 can propel it without pedaling, both to 20 mph; class 3 assists only while pedaling, to 28 mph
From December 1, 2026, riders and passengers under 18 on a class 3 must wear a helmet meeting federal safety standards
Not a motor vehicle: no driver's license, registration or insurance
The rider has the duties of a vehicle driver under the traffic laws

From December 1, 2026, it may be ridden on all roadways, bicycle lanes and multiuse paths, except where a city or county restricts it, or the Department of Natural and Cultural Resources does in state parks and historic sites
From December 1, 2026, cities and counties may restrict classes and set speed limits on multiuse paths and sidewalks, and may require helmets for riders and passengers under 18 on class 1 and class 2
One that exceeds these limits falls under moped rules, which require registration, insurance, a helmet and a rider 16 or older
